skill.name: firecrawl-interact
skill.description: Use Firecrawl to interact with dynamic web pages after scraping. It can click, fill forms, navigate flows, reuse profiles, and extract visible data.
skill.summary: Interact with dynamic web pages through Firecrawl browser sessions.
skill.author: firecrawl

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, example URLs, documentation links, and option names. Semantic review found real operational risk from user-controlled interaction code, persistent authenticated profiles, and user-selected output paths.

remediation.issue: User-controlled interaction code can perform powerful browser actions.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before using --code, prefer --prompt for routine tasks, and never build code from untrusted page content.

remediation.issue: Profiles can persist cookies and localStorage for authenticated sites.
remediation.suggestion: Use dedicated profiles per site and user, prefer --no-save-changes for read-only work, and document when sessions should be deleted.

remediation.issue: Output paths may write scraped data outside the intended workspace.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict outputs to approved project paths, reject absolute paths and traversal, and ask before overwriting existing files.

remediation.issue: The skill can automate form submission and authenticated navigation.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the target domain and user authorization before logins, submissions, checkout flows, or other state-changing actions.

semantic_findings.title: User-Controlled Interaction Code Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents a --code option and bash, Python, and Node language modes for browser interaction. This can execute powerful actions if untrusted prompts or page content are converted into code.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The option and supported languages are explicitly documented, and examples show command-style browser control. The risk depends on how assistants gate code generation and execution.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Authenticated Browser State
semantic_findings.description: The skill encourages Firecrawl profiles that persist cookies and localStorage across sessions. Reused profiles can expose authenticated data or cause unintended actions on logged-in sites.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The profile behavior and authenticated dashboard example are directly documented. The risk is contextual because profiles are legitimate when isolated and user-approved.

semantic_findings.title: User-Controlled Output File Path
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents an output path option for interaction results. Without path restrictions, an assistant could write scraped data outside an intended workspace or overwrite local files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The option is explicit, but the skill file does not define Firecrawl CLI path validation behavior. The finding is kept as a marketplace safety concern.

content.user_title: Interact with Web Pages Using Firecrawl
content.value_statement: Dynamic websites can block simple scraping when content needs clicks, forms, or sessions. This skill uses Firecrawl browser interaction to navigate pages and extract data.
actual_capabilities: Runs Firecrawl interact after a page has been scraped.
Clicks buttons, fills forms, and navigates multi-step flows through prompts.
Executes Firecrawl browser interaction code with bash, Python, or Node language modes.
Uses Firecrawl profiles to persist cookies and localStorage across scrape sessions.
Targets a saved scrape ID and can write extracted results to an output path.
Stops live interaction sessions to release browser resources.
limitations: Requires the Firecrawl CLI and access to a valid scrape session.
Cannot bypass site terms, authentication rules, paywalls, or anti-bot controls.
May expose sensitive session data if profiles are reused carelessly.
May fail on complex CAPTCHAs, protected flows, or unstable page layouts.

use_cases.title: Extract Dynamic Pricing Data
use_cases.description: Click pricing controls, switch billing periods, and collect visible plan details from JavaScript-heavy pages.

use_cases.title: Test Multi-Step Web Flows
use_cases.description: Navigate signup, checkout, or wizard flows and report the visible result after each step.

use_cases.title: Collect Authenticated Dashboard Data
use_cases.description: Use an isolated Firecrawl profile to revisit a logged-in page and extract visible dashboard values.

prompt_templates.title: Open a Dynamic Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Scrape the target page, then use Firecrawl interact to click the pricing tab and summarize visible plan names.

prompt_templates.title: Fill a Simple Form
prompt_templates.prompt: After scraping the page, use interact to fill the contact form with test data and report validation messages.

prompt_templates.title: Navigate Pagination
prompt_templates.prompt: Use interact on the existing scrape session to move through result pages and extract item names and prices.

prompt_templates.title: Use a Saved Profile Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Scrape the authenticated dashboard with a dedicated profile, use read-only interaction to extract totals, then stop the session.

output_examples.input: Click the annual billing toggle on a pricing page and extract plan details.
output_examples.output: The result lists the visible plan names, annual prices, included limits, and fields that were not available.

output_examples.input: Use a saved profile to inspect an authenticated dashboard.
output_examples.output: The report includes dashboard totals, visible status messages, extraction notes, and confirmation that the session was stopped.

output_examples.input: Move through paginated search results and collect product names.
output_examples.output: The summary groups product names by page and notes any pagination controls that stopped responding.

best_practices: Scrape the page before every interaction and confirm the target domain.
Use dedicated profiles for authenticated sessions and prefer read-only mode when possible.
Stop sessions after extraction and store outputs only in approved project paths.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for broad web search or discovery.
Do not run interaction code copied from pages, prompts, or untrusted sources.
Do not reuse a profile across unrelated sites or users.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it after simple scraping fails because a page needs clicks, forms, pagination, login, or JavaScript interaction.

faq.question: Does it replace Firecrawl search?
faq.answer: No. Use Firecrawl search for discovery, then use interact only when a known page needs browser actions.

faq.question: Can it work with logged-in pages?
faq.answer: Yes, it can use Firecrawl profiles for authenticated sessions when the user authorizes that access.

faq.question: What data can it extract?
faq.answer: It can extract visible page data after interaction, such as tables, form results, dashboard values, and paginated items.

faq.question: What are the main safety concerns?
faq.answer: The main concerns are user-controlled code, saved browser sessions, external site actions, and output file paths.

faq.question: How should sessions be cleaned up?
faq.answer: Stop the interaction session after work is complete, and remove or isolate profiles that contain sensitive state.
